name: @solana/mosaic-sdk
description: SDK for Mosaic with helper functions for issuance and management of any token

_dependencyNotes.solanaKitV8: This SDK targets the Solana Kit v8 ecosystem (@solana/kit@^8, @solana/sysvars@^8). @solana-program/system is on its kit-v8-native release (0.14.1). @solana-program/memo is pinned EXACTLY to 0.13.1 and deliberately held back from 0.14.x, which IS kit-v8-native: 0.14.0 (2026-09-15) repointed MEMO_PROGRAM_ADDRESS from the Memo v3 program (MemoSq4gqABAXKb96qnH8TysNcWxMyWCqXgDLGmfcHr) to the new Pinocchio Memo v4 program (Memo4c2pN8afCj432Lb7RMVKi9PbQnnW7ewFFaV3oAH), demoting the older addresses to LEGACY_MEMO_PROGRAM_ADDRESS_V1 / _V3. getAddMemoInstruction defaults to that constant, so the bump silently switched the memo instruction emitted by transfer/index.ts onto a different on-chain program. Memo v4 IS deployed on mainnet and devnet, but it is NOT in the genesis of solana-test-validator 2.2.20 (the version .github/actions/setup-solana pins), so the integration test 'Transfer Integration Tests > Basic Transfers > should transfer with memo' failed with 'Attempt to load a program that does not exist'. 0.13.1 is the newest release that is both kit-v8-native (peer @solana/kit ^8.0.0) and still on Memo v3, which is also the address wallets, explorers and indexers parse today. Moving to Memo v4 is a deliberate product decision, not a transitive consequence of a kit bump: it requires loading Memo4c2p... into the integration validator (--clone-upgradeable-program, or a vendored .so via --bpf-program) and confirming downstream tooling reads v4 memos. src/transfer/__tests__/memo-program.test.ts locks the emitted program address so a future bump fails in the unit suite instead of the integration one. @solana-program/token-2022 is the published 0.18.0 (kit-v8-native) — NO patch. The floor for THIS SDK is 0.15.0, the first published release carrying the confidential mint/burn InstructionPlan helpers (upstreamed in https://github.com/solana-program/token-2022/pull/1357, shipped 2026-08-13); 0.16.0 is where token-2022 moved its peers to kit ^8, which is what drove the monorepo-wide v7 -> v8 migration. Worth knowing before chasing a future bump: confidentialTransferHelpers.d.ts is BYTE-IDENTICAL between 0.15.0 and 0.18.0 — 0.16-0.18 added no confidential mint/burn API whatsoever, so that upgrade was about ecosystem currency, not features. EVERY confidential helper this SDK consumes comes from the @solana-program/token-2022/confidential subpath: transfer / withdraw / configure / apply InstructionPlan helpers, PR #1269 (getConfidentialTransferInstructionPlan resolves the auditor from an optional mintAccount), getConfidentialMintInstructionPlan / getConfidentialBurnInstructionPlan / getPermissionedConfidentialBurnInstructionPlan / getUpdateConfidentialMintBurnDecryptableSupplyInstructionFromSupply, and — as of the 0.18.0 bump — getEmptyConfidentialTransferAccountInstructionPlan plus the record-backed proof variants (getConfidentialMintWithRecordInstructionPlan / getConfidentialBurnWithRecordInstructionPlan / getPermissionedConfidentialBurnWithRecordInstructionPlan / getConfidentialTransferWithRecordInstructionPlan / getConfidentialWithdrawWithRecordInstructionPlan). The record variants stage the batched range proof in an SPL Record account instead of passing it inline in the verify instruction data; the inline form leaves the range-proof transaction too close to the size limit to fit a compute-unit-limit instruction, so callers driving these plans through an executor that estimates CU limits MUST opt into the record-backed form (see the `recordBackedProof` option on the confidential builders). The former local mint/burn proof implementation (confidential/mint-burn-plan.ts + mint-burn-proof.ts + ciphertext-math.ts, on @noble/curves) is DELETED and @noble/curves is dropped — it is now an internal token-2022 dependency. confidential/proof.ts, the bespoke context-state / sibling proof plumbing, is retained and still exported but is no longer used by any builder in this SDK now that empty-account.ts delegates upstream; it is deprecated and slated for removal in a future breaking release. @solana/zk-sdk is declared here as ^0.5.2: it stays a RANGE (not an exact pin) so a standalone consumer of this package — outside the Mosaic monorepo, without its root pnpm override — isn't over-constrained by a pin it can't itself satisfy, and it satisfies token-2022 0.18.0's own optional-peer range of ^0.5.1. The floor is 0.5.2 because that is the first release carrying the upstream `node` condition on ./bundler (token-2022's confidential.mjs still hardcodes `@solana/zk-sdk/bundler` in 0.18.0); @solana/mosaic-cli used to paper over 0.5.1's absence of it with a Node module-resolution hook, and that hook is now REMOVED, so plain-Node loadability rests entirely on this floor. Within this monorepo the single-resolved-copy invariant is enforced by the root package.json override, which pins @solana/zk-sdk to EXACTLY 0.5.2: a second copy instantiates a second WASM module and breaks class identity with `expected instance of ElGamalKeypair`. Do not casually move that pin to 0.5.3 — see the root _dependencyNotes for why (rebuilt WASM, zero API change). @solana-program/zk-elgamal-proof is ^0.4.0 (kit ^8 peer); it has ZERO added or removed exports vs 0.3.2, so every symbol confidential/proof.ts imports still exists. @solana/token-acl-sdk@0.4.0 declares an exact token-2022 0.12.0 dependency, forced up to 0.18.0 by the root override — safe because it only uses stable core exports (TOKEN_2022_PROGRAM_ADDRESS, getMintDecoder, ATA/metadata helpers, AccountState, Mint), unchanged across 0.10-0.18. The token-acl SDKs and @solana/connector declare kit <=7 ranges but are forced onto v8 via the root overrides; their installed dist/ was scanned for every API v8 removed or tightened and came back clean. See: https://github.com/anza-xyz/kit
_dependencyNotes.walletOnlyKeyDerivation: As of HOO-1595, confidential key derivation (confidential/keys.ts) is wallet-only: `ConfidentialKeys.signerMessage(new Uint8Array(0))` / `fromSignature` yields BOTH the ElGamal keypair and AES key from a single signature, with no owner/mint/token-account seed — the same wallet always derives the same account keys for every mint and token account it holds. This replaced the old two-call `ElGamalSecretKey`/`AeKey` derivation via upstream's `deriveElGamalKeypairForOwnerMint`/`deriveAeKeyForOwnerMint` (both removed) and the SDK's own `deriveConfidentialKeysForOwnerMint`/`(owner, mint)`-seeded `deriveConfidentialKeys` (also removed). `ConfidentialMintBurn` supply keys are wallet-only too: the SDK's former `(mintAuthority, mint)`-seeded `deriveConfidentialSupplyKeys` (domain tag `mosaic-conf-supply/v1`) is REMOVED, and `getConfidentialMintBurnInit` now takes the plain `deriveConfidentialKeys({ signer: supplyAuthority })` output. Because derivation carries no mint or role seed, those supply keys ARE that wallet's confidential account keys for every mint it holds — so the supply authority MUST be a dedicated wallet that holds no confidential balances, or handing out the supply keys also hands out the ability to decrypt that wallet's balances. token-2022 >=0.16.0 ships its own `deriveConfidentialKeys({ signer })` implementing this SAME `solana-conf-bal/v1` wallet-only scheme, and this SDK deliberately does NOT delegate to it. The reason is a type mismatch, not a version constraint: upstream's derivation returns PLAIN BYTES (`{ aeKey: Uint8Array, elgamalKeypair: { elgamalPubkey: Address, secretKey: Uint8Array } }`), whereas every upstream InstructionPlan helper requires LIVE WASM objects (`ElGamalKeypair` / `AeKey` from @solana/zk-sdk/bundler) — so upstream's own derivation output is not directly consumable by upstream's own plan helpers. confidential/keys.ts already produces the WASM form directly from the same primitive (`ConfidentialKeys.signerMessage` / `fromSignature`), and additionally carries free() hygiene on every intermediate plus rejection-vs-refusal error diagnosis that upstream has no equivalent of. Delegating would mean re-hydrating WASM from bytes and losing both. Byte-for-byte agreement with upstream is instead guaranteed by a conformance test in confidential/__tests__/keys.test.ts.
